body_markdown:
## Operational Essentials: Product Listing, Fulfillment, and Account Health


### Listing Your Products: Catalog Setup and Inventory Management


A dependable catalog includes the product title, category, brand information, variations, dimensions, weight, price, images, video, and compliance details. Use language that matches the item customers receive. Show multiple product angles, identify included components, and state sizing or compatibility information. Inaccurate attributes can increase returns, complaints, and visibility limits.


Set available quantities conservatively, account for units reserved in pending orders, and define a reorder point based on supplier lead time. Review variation-level inventory during promotions or livestreams. Pause an option before overselling creates cancellations, and maintain SKU codes, warehouse locations, carton details, and replenishment dates in one shared record.


### Fulfillment Strategies: Fulfilled by TikTok (FBT) vs. Seller Shipping


Your fulfillment choice affects storage, handling, delivery speed, customer experience, and control. Fulfilled by TikTok, or FBT, can reduce picking, packing, and carrier-handoff work when eligible inventory is placed within the program. Seller shipping keeps inventory and dispatch decisions in your facility and may suit merchants with established warehouse processes or specialized packaging needs. Confirm current eligibility, service coverage, fees, inbound requirements, and return procedures inside Seller Center before selecting a method.


Operational factor FBT Seller shipping


Inventory location Stock is sent to designated fulfillment facilities Stock remains in the seller’s warehouse or third-party facility


Daily handling Program processes eligible pick, pack, and shipment tasks Seller manages order processing and carrier handoff


Control Less direct control over packing workflow Greater control over packaging and dispatch procedures


Planning requirement Forecast inbound stock and replenishment needs Maintain labor, supplies, carrier pickups, and warehouse capacity


### Mastering Fulfillment SLAs: Avoiding Penalties and Account Suspension


Fulfillment service-level agreements measure whether orders are processed, shipped, delivered, canceled, and handled within stated requirements. Review current shipping and performance policies in Seller Center because thresholds and enforcement can change by market, category, and program. Monitor unshipped orders, carrier scans, failed deliveries, cancellations, and buyer messages each business day.


Keep shipping supplies available, set accurate handling times, test carrier pickup routines, and pause listings when inventory cannot support promised dispatch. Record tracking numbers at handoff and investigate missing scans. Do not mark an order shipped before carrier acceptance. Repeated late shipment, seller cancellation, invalid tracking, or delivery failures can reduce account standing and may lead to restrictions or suspension.


### Monitoring Account Health: Key Metrics and Best Practices


Monitor order defect signals, late shipment rate, cancellation rate, valid tracking, return reasons, refund activity, customer response time, product violations, and policy notices. Segment metrics by SKU, warehouse, carrier, fulfillment method, and sales source to identify whether a problem comes from an item, process, location, or campaign.

Pair those signals with a weekly operations review and assign an owner and correction deadline for each major variance.
